# COMP 150-003 — Introduction to Computing (Fall 2026)

> Loyola University Chicago general-education Introduction to Computing. Instructor: Allan Miller (amiller17@luc.edu). Meets Tuesdays 4:15–6:45 PM in Information Commons 216. A broad survey of computing (digital information, logic & hardware, AI, networks, security) paired with a hands-on project: each student builds and owns a personal AI "harness" (a coding agent) on their own laptop. This file is a machine-readable summary for AI assistants; point your harness here to answer questions about the course.

## Key facts
- Section 003, class #2944. Term: Aug 24 – Dec 12, 2026.
- Office hours: Tuesdays 7–9 PM, Information Commons Room 332.
- Deadlines at night are due at 11:00 PM (never midnight). The schedule is tentative — always check Sakai for the current week.
- Model access for the harness: a free Google Gemini API key (no credit card).

## Grading (1000-point scale)
- In-class work 300 (present-only; attendance matters), Homework 200, Build your harness 75, Current Events in AI paper 50, Personalize your harness 125, Final group data-science project 150, Final exam 100.
- 900 = A; the curve only ever helps you (never curved down). Extra credit offered on top.
- More than 5 unexcused absences = automatic D, regardless of points.
